Given:

$$w = \text{image of } z \text{ under rotation } \frac{\pi}{4} \text{ around } c$$

The formula for rotating a complex number $z$ about a point $c$ by an angle $\theta$ is:
$$w = c + e^{i\theta}(z - c)$$

First, we calculate the difference $z - c$:
$$z - c = \left(2 + \sqrt{2} - (3 + 3\sqrt{2})\right)i - (2 - 3i)$$
$$z - c = (2 + \sqrt{2} - 2) + i(-(3 + 3\sqrt{2}) - (-3))$$
$$z - c = \sqrt{2} + i(-3 - 3\sqrt{2} + 3)$$
$$z - c = \sqrt{2} - 3\sqrt{2}i$$
$$z - c = \sqrt{2}(1 - 3i)$$

Next, we apply the rotation by angle $\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$ (which is $45^\circ$). We know that:
$$e^{i\theta} = \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} + i\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{1 + i}{\sqrt{2}}$$

$$w = c + e^{i\theta}(z - c)$$

$$w = 2 - 3i + (1 - 2i + 3)$$
$$w = 2 - 3i + 4 - 2i$$
$$w = 6 - 5i$$
